questions.qtext:
A node $p$ in a control flow graph(CFG) $\text{N}$ dominates a node $q$ if every path from the entry node to $q$ goes through $p$. We say that node $p$ is a dominator of node $q.$
The dominator set of node $q,\; \text{DOM(}q),$ is formed by all nodes that dominate $q.$ By definition, each node dominates itself, therefore, $\mathrm{q} \in \operatorname{DOM}(\mathrm{q})$

  • $\mathrm{p}$ dominates $\mathrm{q}$, written $\mathrm{p} \leq \mathrm{q}$, i.e. $\mathrm{p} \in \operatorname{DOM}(\mathrm{q})$.
  • $\mathrm{p}$ properly (strictly) dominates $\mathrm{q}$, written $\mathrm{p}<\mathrm{q}$ if $\mathrm{p} \leq \mathrm{q}$ and $\mathrm{p} \neq \mathrm{q}$.
  • $\mathrm{p}$ immediately (or directly) dominates $\mathrm{q}$, if $\mathrm{p}<\mathrm{q}$ and there is no node $t$ such that $\mathrm{p}<\mathrm{t}<\mathrm{q}$.

We say $p$ is the immediate dominator of $q$ and write $p=\operatorname{IDOM}(q)$
